text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Rotterdam's plans for second Maasvlakte industrial site and harbour basin unnecessary - Central Planning Bureau. (p1)
- Vendex International plans to buy shoe, sport and clothing retail chain Scapino with 160 outlets. (p1)
- The Dutch government in 1993 could not refuse to allow so-called techno-lease agreements between Philips and Rabobank . (p1)
- Soft loans worth 1.75 billion guilders, promised by Wim Kok in 1995 to make Dutch companies competitive in China, have yet to be granted. (p1)
- Talks between food company Nutricia and Friesland Dairy Foods on possible transfer of operations have halted. (p3)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel to sell nylon activities of Brazilian unit Cobafi to DuPont. (p3)
- Iberia airlines president Javier de Irala calls an alliance with KLM "a very concrete option". (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Labour party PvdA, D66 and Christian Democrats CDA keep policy in favour of NATO in Eastern Europe. (p1)
- Forwarding agents dissatisfied with Royal Dutch Airlines freight unit KLM Cargo's service. (p2)
- Nature conservationist group maintains its opposition to a residential area on articifical islands near Amsterdam. (p4)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Transavia Airlines Boeing 737 makes successful emergency landing with in Nuremberg, Germany. (p1)
- Nutricia withdraws 2,000 - 3,000 packets of baby food from the French market. (p1)
- Consortium headed by machine maker Stork is competing to build powerplant on Curacao. (p13)
- Akzo Nobel settles long running conflict with U.S. company Intercat. (p13)
TROUW
- Some 30,000 pigs have to be killed in province of North Brabant due to outbreak of swine fever. (p1)
- Employees and unions in the building sector reach agreement on temp workers. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Health minister Els Borst want measures in Europe against forging of medicines. (p1)
- Food and detergent company Unilever sells its German fish shop chain Nordsee, says British newspaper the Observer. (p11)
